published_results.metric: cold-start system-prompt token overhead (--minimal install profile vs full)
published_results.notes: No measurement script, tokenizer, or raw count committed; repeated across CHANGELOG, release notes and localized READMEs with '~' approximations.

published_results.claim: | GSD share of a 200k 1% budget | ~60% | ... Estimated description tokens (÷4) | ~1,196 |
published_results.metric: share of Claude Code's default skill-listing budget consumed by GSD skill descriptions (chars/4 token estimate)
published_results.value: ~60%; 4,787 description chars, ~1,196 estimated tokens across 66 skills
published_results.notes: Committed per-skill audit JSON backs the counts, but the memo says the extraction script is not in scripts/ ('one-shot snapshot', line 252). Token figure is a chars/4 estimate, not tokenizer output.

published_results.metric: static prompt overhead reduction (context-window-aware prompt thinning)
published_results.notes: Stated as a feature purpose/target; no measurement.

published_results.notes: Changelog statement; verifiable only by diffing git history, no method given.

summary: The English README is now only a 'GSD Has Moved' redirect, and the project publishes no measured outcome of its workflow (no task success, quality or 'context rot' evaluation). Its numbers are prompt-size figures: '~12k -> ~700 tokens' for --minimal and '~40%' prompt thinning, stated without method, plus a skill-budget memo backed by a committed one-shot audit JSON whose extraction script is not in the repo.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
